description: Early indicators show accelerated job losses in administrative, legal support and mid-tier tech roles across several member states, with sectoral studies attributing displacement to AI adoption in large firms. The data is not yet public consensus, but trade unions and national labour offices begin sounding alarms, feeding into upcoming political debates. This could evolve into broader socio-political backlash if unchecked.

European AI researchers and engineers increasingly accept positions with U.S. frontier labs offering higher salaries, faster compute, and greater strategic influence. This quiet exodus slows the EU's ability to build sovereign capability despite existing infrastructure. The trend becomes visible in hiring reports and academic mobility data, raising alarms in Brussels about long-term dependence.
